name: Mordecai
description: Esther's relative living at the time of Exile and Return

points: Now in Shushan the palace there was a certain Jew, whose name was Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite: Mordecai and Esther were of the tribe of Benjamin.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: Esther was the daughter of Mordecai's uncle: they were cousins, not uncle and niece; do not say that. Her parents died, and Mordecai took her for his own daughter and raised her up.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: Mordecai brought up Hadassah, that is Esther, his uncle's daughter, for she had neither father nor mother, and the maid was fair and beautiful, and when her parents were dead he took her for his own daughter. Esther is a Persian name after Ishtar, which is one reason the old rabbis said little of this book.

note.label: Esther 2: Esther Made Queen and Mordecai Uncovers the Plot

points: Esther had not shown her people nor her kindred, for Mordecai had charged her not to show it, and Mordecai walked every day before the court of the women's house to know how Esther did. She is racially ambiguous, a daughter of Israel who could not be told at a glance to be black or Hispanic, which is why we go by whether a spirit bears witness with this Bible.

note.label: Esther 2: Esther Made Queen and Mordecai Uncovers the Plot

points: When Esther's turn came, the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai who took her for his daughter, she required nothing but what Hegai the keeper of the women appointed, and Esther obtained favour in the sight of all who looked upon her.

note.label: Esther 2: Esther Made Queen and Mordecai Uncovers the Plot

points: When the virgins were gathered the second time, Mordecai sat in the king's gate, and Esther had not yet showed her kindred nor her people as Mordecai had charged her.

note.label: Esther 2: Esther Made Queen and Mordecai Uncovers the Plot

points: Esther had not shewed her people nor her kindred: for Mordecai had charged her that she should not shew it. Do not tell anyone that you are an Israelite. The Persians are a dark people themselves, and from Esther's look you could not tell what she was; she could pass, and she kept the commandment of Mordecai, like as when she was brought up with him.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: Esther did the commandment of Mordecai just as when she was brought up with him, still subject to her uncle and still listening to him even after she was made queen.

note.label: Esther 2: Esther Made Queen and Mordecai Uncovers the Plot

points: Two of the king's chamberlains, of those which kept the door, were wroth, and sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus. And the thing was known to Mordecai, who told it unto Esther the queen; and Esther certified the king thereof in Mordecai's name. Inquisition was made; both were hanged on a tree; and it was written in the book of the chronicles before the king. Mordecai saved the king's life, and it went on record.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: In those days, while Mordecai sat in the king's gate, two of the king's chamberlains that kept the door were wroth and sought to lay hands on king Ahasuerus, plotting a coup against him.

note.label: Esther 2: Esther Made Queen and Mordecai Uncovers the Plot

points: All the king's servants bowed and reverenced Haman, for the king had so commanded; but Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence. It is not our custom to bow to any man.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: They spake daily unto him, and he hearkened not; and they told Haman, to see whether Mordecai's matters would stand: for he had told them that he was a Jew. And when Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not, Haman was full of wrath.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: The servants asked daily why Mordecai transgressed the king's commandment, and he hearkened not, but told them he was a Jew, and they told Haman to see whether Mordecai's matter would stand. We do not bow, the same as the three Hebrew children did not bow to the image in Babylon, for we pledge allegiance to none but the Most High.

note.label: Esther 3: Haman the Agagite and the Decree to Destroy the Jews

points: When Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not nor did him reverence, he was full of wrath, and thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone once they had shown him the people of Mordecai.

note.label: Esther 3: Haman the Agagite and the Decree to Destroy the Jews

points: And he thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone: Haman sought to destroy all the Jews that were throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, for what one Jew would not do. Why all of them? Remember what king Saul was sent to do to Amalek. Haman's people kept the records; he knew Mordecai's line, the line of Kish, was the line sent to destroy his forefathers. Esau forgave Jacob, but his children hold the grudge from generation to generation. They do not forget; we do.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: Haman sought to destroy all the Jews throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, the people of Mordecai, not one man only. Because Mordecai would not bow, Edom's hatred sought a death sentence for the entire nation, seeking to erase us out of history.

note.label: Esther 3: Haman the Agagite and the Decree to Destroy the Jews

points: When Mordecai perceived all that was done he rent his clothes, put on sackcloth with ashes, went out into the midst of the city and cried with a loud and bitter cry, and came before the king's gate, for none might enter it clothed with sackcloth.

note.label: Esther 4: Mordecai Charges Esther for Such a Time as This

points: Esther's maids and chamberlain told her, and the queen was exceedingly grieved and sent raiment to clothe Mordecai and take away his sackcloth, but he received it not. She sent Hatach, appointed to attend her, to learn what it was and why.

note.label: Esther 4: Mordecai Charges Esther for Such a Time as This

points: Mordecai told Hatach all that had happened and of the money Haman promised to pay for the Jews to be destroyed, and gave him a copy of the decree published in Shushan to show Esther, charging her to go in to the king and make supplication for her people.

note.label: Esther 4: Mordecai Charges Esther for Such a Time as This

points: So Mordecai went his way and did according to all Esther commanded him. She had her mind set right, ready to risk her life for her people.

note.label: Esther 4: Mordecai Charges Esther for Such a Time as This

points: Haman went forth that day joyful and glad of heart, but when he saw Mordecai in the king's gate who stood not up nor moved for him, he was full of indignation, yet refrained himself and went home and called for his friends and Zeresh his wife.

note.label: Esther 5: Esther Finds Favour and Haman Builds the Gallows

points: Then Zeresh his wife and all his friends counselled that a gallows fifty cubits high be made, and on the morrow he should speak to the king that Mordecai be hanged thereon, and then go merrily to the banquet, and the thing pleased Haman and he caused the gallows to be made. It was the wife's idea, for the enemy's women are in cahoots with the work against Israel.

note.label: Esther 5: Esther Finds Favour and Haman Builds the Gallows

points: It was found written that Mordecai had told of Bigthana and Teresh, two chamberlains who sought to lay hand on the king, and yet nothing had been done to honor him for it.

note.label: Esther 6: The King Honors Mordecai

points: The king asked what honor had been done to Mordecai, and his servants answered that there was nothing done for him.

note.label: Esther 6: The King Honors Mordecai

points: The king asked who was in the court, and Haman had just come into the outer court to speak to the king about hanging Mordecai on the gallows he had prepared.

In the previous chapter Haman's wife had told him to make a gallows fifty cubits high and hang Mordecai on it, so Haman was coming to carry out that plan at the very moment the king had learned Mordecai saved his life.

note.label: Esther 6: The King Honors Mordecai

points: The king told Haman to make haste and do exactly as he said to Mordecai the Jew who sat at the king's gate, letting nothing fail of all he had spoken.

note.label: Esther 6: The King Honors Mordecai

points: Haman then took the apparel and the horse, arrayed Mordecai, brought him on horseback through the street, and proclaimed before him. What Haman planned for himself was given to the man he hated. This is how the Most High works, and it should put a smile on your face.

note.label: Esther 6: The King Honors Mordecai

points: Mordecai returned to the king's gate, but Haman hurried to his house mourning with his head covered, and told his wife Zeresh and his friends all that had happened.

note.label: Esther 6: The King Honors Mordecai

points: His wise men and his wife told him that if Mordecai was of the seed of the Jews, before whom he had begun to fall, he would not prevail but would surely fall before him.

note.label: Esther 6: The King Honors Mordecai

points: Harbonah, a chamberlain, told the king of the gallows fifty cubits high that Haman had made for Mordecai, who had spoken good for the king, standing at Haman's house.

note.label: Esther 7: Haman Hanged on His Own Gallows

points: The king commanded Haman be hanged on it, and they hanged Haman on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai, and the king's wrath was pacified. This is the Most High, a man of war, and this is how He moves.

note.label: Esther 7: Haman Hanged on His Own Gallows

points: That day the king gave the house of Haman, the Jews' enemy, to Esther, and Mordecai came before the king, for Esther had told what he was to her.

note.label: Esther 8: The Decree Reversed for the Jews

points: The king took off the ring he had taken from Haman and gave it to Mordecai, and Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman. Everything Haman had was given to Mordecai.

note.label: Esther 8: The Decree Reversed for the Jews

points: The king told Esther and Mordecai that he had given Esther the house of Haman and had hanged Haman for laying hand upon the Jews.
Esther and Mordecai were given the king's authority, so the reputation and word of the king stood behind whatever they wrote.

note.label: Esther 8: The Decree Reversed for the Jews

points: Mordecai went out from the king in royal apparel of blue and white, a great crown of gold, and a garment of fine linen and purple, and the city of Shushan rejoiced and was glad.

note.label: Esther 8: The Decree Reversed for the Jews

points: The Jews gathered in their cities, and no man could withstand them, for the fear of them fell upon all people, and the rulers, lieutenants, deputies, and officers helped the Jews because the fear of Mordecai fell upon them.

note.label: Esther 9: Purim and the Victory of the Jews

points: Mordecai was great in the king's house and his fame went throughout all the provinces, and this man waxed greater and greater. Though Esther was queen, she was still subject to Mordecai, the man of Israel who wrote the edict.

note.label: Esther 9: Purim and the Victory of the Jews

points: Mordecai wrote these things and sent letters to all the Jews near and far to establish that they keep the fourteenth and fifteenth days of Adar yearly.

note.label: Esther 9: Purim and the Victory of the Jews

points: Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew wrote with all authority to confirm this second letter of Purim.

note.label: Esther 9: Purim and the Victory of the Jews
